subject: Dedicated capacity options — sizing matrix and activation playbook
messages:
From: Avery Collins <avery@omniflow.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos@omniflow.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity proposal — initial sizing and timeline

Grace,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Per our call, here's a concise summary of OmniFlow's expected production needs to include in your dedicated reservation proposal so we can compare commitment tiers.

- Models in scope: Llama-2-70B (quant 4/8), custom reranker (small 1B).
- Avg concurrent requests: 350 sessions/day; peak concurrency pattern: 8am-11am PST and 6pm-9pm PST.
- Token profile: 1.5k avg input + 600 token generation; ~1.1M tokens/day current, targeting ~4.5M tokens/day in 3 months.
- Latency target: p95 < 220ms for the generator; p50 < 90ms for reranker.
- Business start target: early July 2027 for pilot to prod ramp.
- Constraints: tight cost control (targeting ~25% lower unit-cost than on-demand), required 99.9% uptime SLA, and SOC2-suitable audit logs.

As far as flexibility, we can commit to a 12 month reserved contract but need a smooth ramp schedule and the ability to burst for seasonal demand. Please include recommended min GPU floors, an activation/ramp timeline, suggested burst lanes, and an outline of warm-start/pre-warm strategies.

I've attached a sample traffic pattern export (omniflow-traffic-sample.csv).

Thanks,
Avery

—
Avery Collins
Head of Platform
OmniFlow AI
avery@omniflow.ai

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Avery Collins <avery@omniflow.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos@omniflow.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — initial sizing and timeline

Avery — thanks for the clear summary and for the sample traffic. I've sketched three differentiated reservation options below that balance your cost target, uptime, and burst needs. Attaching a one-page matrix (reserve-options-grid.pdf).

Option A — Anchored Floor (recommended for predictable cost):
- Minimum committed: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (anchored floor)
- Burst: autoscale to 60 GPUs via reserved burst buffer + on-demand fallback
- Ramp: Pilot (Jul) 24 -> 36 by Sep -> 48 by Dec -> 72 by Mar 2028
- Notes: Strong unit-cost reduction, longer warm-up for tail-latency-sensitive traffic.

Option B — Stage-and-Burst (cost-flexible):
- Minimum committed: 12 GPUs for Q1 pilot
- Burst lanes: guaranteed 36 reserved burst GPUs + on-demand up to 90 if needed
- Ramp: 12 -> 24 (month 2) -> 36 (month 4), conditional on usage triggers
- Notes: Lower initial spend, higher operational burst exposure.

Option C — Pilot-first (fast experiment):
- Minimum committed: 6 GPUs (pilot) with aggressive quantization suggestions
- Ramp: manual step increases tied to milestones (demo -> alpha -> beta)
- Notes: Best for product validation, limited economy of scale.

Common mechanics across options:
- Warm pool: maintain 10–15% pre-warmed instances within reserved pool during business hours to reduce startup latency.
- KV/prefix caching: we will enable request-level KV caching for repeat prompts to shave token cost.
- Rollout: Canary model pinning + auto-fallback to a smaller-quantized variant if capacity constrained.

Next steps: can we do a 30-minute technical review with Ben (serve/runtime) and Karthik (product) on Wed or Thu to align on kernel/quantization tradeoffs and finalize the committed floor? After that we’ll issue a draft SOW + MPU (monthly pricing) with estimated unit economics.

Grace

—
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Lead, Dedicated Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Avery Collins <avery@omniflow.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — initial sizing and timeline

Adding a few technical considerations to the options Grace shared — pulled from perf sims against the traffic sample.

- Baseline sizing rationale: Llama-2-70B quant 4 typically delivers ~0.9–1.1 tokens/sec per A100-equivalent when served with our optimized kernels and continuous batching at 1.5k seq lengths. Given your 4.5M tokens/day target, steady-state compute maps to ~30–35 GPUs, with peaks needing the burst buffer.

- Warm pool sizing: recommend reserving ~4–6 GPUs as hot pool during the 8am-11am and 6pm-9pm windows (these should be part of the committed floor rather than ephemeral on-demand to satisfy latency SLOs).

- Batching and autoscale: set continuous-batch target to 8–12 requests/batch for the generator and tighter batching for reranker. Autoscale should be governed by request queue depth + p95 latency triggers to avoid oscillation.

- Quantization and kernel tradeoffs: 4-bit quant is attractive for cost but expect a 5–12% p95 latency increase vs int8 on some sequences. We can automate trials in pilot to pick the sweet spot.

- Storage/I/O and KV cache: because OmniFlow has many repeat prompts, enabling a prefix cache will reduce compute by ~8–15% in our estimate. Plan the LRU cache size for the first 90 days based on the attached sim (batching-sim.xlsx).

Attachments: batching-sim.xlsx (simulation), kernel-profile.json (sample perf knobs).

If you want, I can run a short 2-hour perf run on a staging pool (we'll reserve a small pay-for-play slot) to validate Option A assumptions before we commit.

Ben
Head of Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Avery Collins <avery@omniflow.ai>, Carlos Mendes <carlos@omniflow.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity proposal — initial sizing and timeline

Team — wrapping this thread with a recommended path that balances OmniFlow's cost target and risk tolerance. Please treat as our suggested default for the SOW.

Recommendation (final):
- Committed floor: 24 GPUs (A100-equivalent) starting July 1, 2027. This covers minimal steady-state and maintains SLA.
- Fast ramp: add 12 GPUs by Sep 1, 2027 and +12 by Dec 1, 2027 (48 by year-end). Target 72 GPUs by Mar 1, 2028 if usage growth meets the agreed triggers.
- Burst policy: 36 reserved burst GPUs available immediately; on-demand fallback beyond that up to 96 (charged at on-demand uplift).
- Warm-start: include a 6 GPU hot pool that maps to your peak windows; these are part of the committed floor to keep p95 consistent.
- Billing & credits: offer a smoothing credit (5% over first three months) to ease activation burn and a one-time warmup credit if staging perf run is executed.

Operational items for the mutual action plan:
1) Wed 30 Mar — 30m technical review (Ben leads).
2) Mon 4 Apr — send draft SOW + pricing MPU (Grace).
3) Tue 12 Apr — signed SOW target / legal kickoff (Avery & legal ops).

Avery/Carlos — please confirm Wed 30 availability and whether the warmup perf run is useful; we'll schedule and lock the staging slot if you want it (we can run it in mid-April). Once you confirm, Grace will publish the SOW draft and pricing sheet.

Karthik
VP Product
Redwood Inference
